entries.updatedReason: caimu.org.kg remains completely unreachable (connection failure on both http:// and https://, no response). Checked the Wayback Machine (archive.org/wayback/available) for this exact domain with and without a timestamp filter; it returns zero archived snapshots, so the archive.org fallback technique is not available for this institution. No press/media alternate domain was identified. Still-hold.

camuf.uz is a client-side-rendered Nuxt.js single-page app: the server returns an identical empty HTML shell for every path, including guessed asset paths (e.g. /logo.png returns HTTP 200 with the SPA shell, not an image), so no logo/cover URL could be extracted from the static markup. Its Wayback Machine snapshot is the same JS-only shell. The one genuine static asset on the domain, /favicon.ico, was downloaded and inspected directly: it only contains 16x16 and 32x32 icon sizes, too low-resolution to serve as a verified institutional logo. Still-hold.

Confirmed the first-pass finding: WDOMS records this school as renamed/absorbed into Akfa University Medical School post-2023. This is an unresolved rename/identity situation, not a missing-asset problem - any current official media would carry Akfa University branding rather than the historical "Central Asian University" name in this catalogue record. Needs an editorial decision (merge into the Akfa record, or keep as a distinct historical entry) before any logo or cover is sourced. No media proposed.

entries.updatedReason: The historical domain csmu.ru no longer resolves. Its likely successor domain, chelsma.ru, 301-redirects to susmu.su, whose homepage title is "Южно-Уральский государственный медицинский университет" (South Ural State Medical University), repeatedly referencing Chelyabinsk in its body text. This indicates Chelyabinsk State Medical University/Academy was renamed to South Ural State Medical University. Flagging as an unresolved rename/identity issue - the catalogue record needs a decision on whether it should be merged into or redirected to a South Ural State Medical University record before assigning media, rather than silently relabelling the renamed institution's assets under the old name. No media sourced.
